# Testing Guide for 2D&D

See [`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md) and
[`docs/testing.md`](../../../docs/testing.md) for the release gate, CI ownership,
and browser-test setup.

Write comprehensive game-mechanics tests with Vitest. Use the committed
Playwright suite only for high-value Phaser browser flows that cannot be proven
through pure logic tests.

Use `playwright.desktop.config.ts` for the production-like Electron flow. It
must verify the `app://2dnd` origin, sandboxed preload API, fullscreen control,
schema-v17 save creation/relaunch/continue, Save & Return to Title, title-screen
quit, bounded lifecycle logs, and renderer error cleanliness.

## Testing Philosophy

### What TO Test
✅ Dice probability distributions
✅ Combat calculation accuracy  
✅ Group initiative, formation, targeting, synergies, rewards, and encounter budgets
✅ Player stat progression
✅ XP and leveling formulas
✅ Quest objective counters, prerequisites, rewards, gates, danger rules, and
save normalization
✅ Companion definitions, party progression, transfers, KO/reward rules, and
ranked gambit selection/normalization
✅ Data integrity (monsters, spells, items)
✅ Monster family references, membership, variant differentiation, palette
uniqueness, encounter weights, Codex family completion, and texture-key coverage
✅ Codex knowledge IDs, canonical references, every unlock signal, idempotency,
normalization/migration, search/sort/group behavior, and future-hook isolation
✅ Game logic functions
✅ Seeded layouts and persistent state machines
✅ Non-combat skill-check math, outcomes, and save normalization
✅ Scene-transition event ordering, duplicate guards, and watchdog recovery with
mocked camera/time adapters
✅ Cutscene data integrity, trigger priority, queue recovery, replay immutability,
shared preference normalization/migration, and director cleanup
✅ Runtime hero descriptor normalization, collision-free visual keys, every
cutscene hero-role cue, equipment layer ordering/fallbacks, texture leases, and
current-player rendering across opening, recovery, Chronicle, bosses, and ending
✅ Tutorial content integrity, semantic control references, completion
normalization, progression-aware tip unlocks, and save migration
✅ Feature registry integrity, authoritative reconciliation, irreversible
visibility, dynamic menu/tab filtering, focus clamping, shortcut/touch gating,
debug exclusion, category-specific discovery, and schema-v17 migration
✅ Defeat penalty receipts, once-only Battle resolution, recovered save
round-trips, result-scene continuation, and random/boss parity
✅ Animation state selection, reduced-motion timing, stable actor/target mapping,
once-only completion and cleanup, and family-frame fallback resolution
✅ Semantic mappings, context priority, analog dead zones, repeats, source
switching, duplicate suppression, disconnect/blur cleanup, and control
preference migration
✅ Measured stacks/grids, safe-area clamping, long-string wrapping,
pagination/visible ranges, filtered focus restoration, scaled bounds,
hit-area alignment, and debug/test overlap detection
✅ Alignment boundaries, reputation tiers, clamping, stable-source
idempotency, quest/dialogue/event/trap/combat hooks, shop composition, Codex
milestones, schema-v12 migration, bounded history, and debug commands
✅ Achievement definition integrity, deterministic progress, hidden entries,
idempotent battle/event/social hooks, reconciliation, schema-v13 migration,
one-hit/no-defeat rules, cosmetic titles, debug exclusion, notices, and
authority isolation
✅ Gathering terrain safety, seeded tables, all three state machines,
reduced-motion equivalence, cooldowns, environmental weights, economy, guarded
Battle handoffs, recipe-input isolation, schema-v14 migration, and pending reload
✅ Crafting recipe integrity, alternative material matching, protected/equipped
items, atomic batches, repeated-input suppression, equipment-link upgrades,
ownership, discovery, acquisition tables, anti-arbitrage, achievements, debug
exclusion, authority isolation, schema-v15 migration, and corruption repair
✅ Nautical continent/zone/port/island integrity, pre-boat merchant routes,
boat acquisition/upgrades, embark/disembark safety, sea fog, capped encounters,
weather hazards, Kraken hooks, sea gathering/crafting economy, schema-v16
migration/corruption recovery, debug commands, and browser reload while sailing

### What NOT to Test  
❌ Phaser rendering/graphics
❌ Scene transitions
❌ User input handling
❌ Visual appearance
❌ Animation timing

These exclusions apply to Vitest. The focused `e2e/` suite owns the real-browser
campaign golden path and scene/input integration.

Animation browser coverage should assert debug-state evidence from real action
menus and combat turns for hero, companion, monster, and boss presentation;
spell/ability particles; world/follower/mount gait; boss cutscenes; fainting;
reduced-motion immediate states; and page/console cleanliness.

Battle backdrop browser coverage uses deterministic `/battleview` and
`/backdrop` controls, programmatic depth/bounds/cleanup assertions, and focused
canvas screenshots for group, boss, Kraken, mobile, weather, and high-contrast
combinations. Keep the full biome/time/weather matrix assertion-driven rather
than committing hundreds of redundant images.

Accessibility browser coverage should change settings from both title and
in-game surfaces, assert immediate canvas state, exercise core overlays at every
supported text scale, verify reload persistence, and prove `2dnd_save` is
unchanged by preference updates.

Semantic-controls browser coverage uses mobile/touch emulation and deterministic
standard-gamepad stubs. It covers onboarding and mobile text entry, movement,
overlays, prompt/source switching, Battle action/target confirmation, defeat
recovery, gamepad cursor visibility, portrait/landscape layout, and page/console
cleanliness.

Codex browser coverage follows real exploration, quest, cutscene, item, NPC, and
readable paths; verifies non-blocking feedback, reload persistence, schema-v9
migration, keyboard/touch/gamepad search and filters, 150% text, reduced motion,
and page/console cleanliness.

## Test File Organization

```
tests/
├── dice.test.ts      # Dice rolling utilities
├── combat.test.ts    # Combat mechanics
├── groupCombat.test.ts # Multi-monster combat rules
├── battleActions.test.ts # Pure gambit planning and validation
├── monsterGroups.test.ts # Group templates and generation
├── monsterFamilies.test.ts # Families, variants, Codex derivation, texture keys
├── codexKnowledge.test.ts # World knowledge data, triggers, queries, and hooks
├── partyCombat.test.ts # Stable actor IDs, ally scopes, AI, and result hooks
├── party.test.ts     # Recruitment, progression, transfers, rests, KO/rewards
├── companions.test.ts # Immutable companion definitions and loadouts
├── gambits.test.ts   # Ranked conditions/actions/targets and normalization
├── followers.test.ts # Pure non-blocking follower trail updates
├── player.test.ts    # Player systems
├── traps.test.ts     # Dungeon trap placement, checks, and effects
├── quests.test.ts    # Quest progression and integrity
├── skillChecks.test.ts # Exploration/dialogue checks
├── reputation.test.ts # Alignment, reputation, integrations, and migration policy
├── achievements.test.ts # Definitions, progress, hooks, titles, and migration policy
├── cutscenes.test.ts # Cutscene data, triggers, queue, and director lifecycle
├── accessibility.test.ts # Shared preference normalization, migration, and persistence
├── input.test.ts # Semantic mappings, contexts, repeats, cleanup, and suppression
├── tutorial.test.ts # Tutorial content, completion, and unlocked Tips
├── featureDiscovery.test.ts # Registry, reconciliation, filtering, debug, migration
├── gathering.test.ts # Gathering data, state machines, rewards, and save rules
├── crafting.test.ts # Recipes, transactions, discovery, economy, and save rules
├── cutsceneSceneTransition.test.ts # Generic Cutscene scene contracts
├── defeatSceneTransition.test.ts # Defeat result continuation contract
├── save.test.ts      # Persistence and migration
└── data.test.ts      # Data validation
```

Quest tests must cover duplicate matching monsters in one group victory,
durable boss reconciliation, optional-objective reward cutoffs, hard-gate
softlock safety, reward idempotency, and flat schema-v4 to nested schema-v5
migration. Map main-quest NPC objectives to live city IDs and require exact
coverage of all 12 cities with stable stage/objective identities.

Tutorial tests must keep Phaser out of pure logic. Assert stable unique IDs,
valid semantic control references, idempotent completion, safe malformed-state
normalization, and exact progression-aware tip unlock sets. The committed
Playwright flow owns automatic presentation, pointer navigation, persisted
completion, `F1`, and Esc-menu access.

## Skill Check Testing

- Pass explicit natural d20 values to `resolveSkillCheck()`; do not depend on
  randomness.
- Verify total-vs-DC behavior, including that natural 1/20 are not automatic.
- Test shop discounts for both successful and failed saved choices.
- Validate NPC identities and chest metadata against live city/map data.
- Test terrain event selection with explicit random values.
- Cover reward bounds, nonlethal damage, save round trips, missing fields, and
  malformed record repair.

## Cutscene Testing

- Validate every stable ID, trigger reference, boss mapping, and completion
  metadata without rendering Phaser.
- Compare immutable before/after snapshots and assert exact simultaneous-trigger
  priority.
- Test that queueing precedes presentation, completion/skip moves pending to
  seen, reload resumes pending, and replay leaves both collections unchanged.
- Cover malformed pending IDs, already-seen pending entries, and completed
  legacy epilogue recovery.
- Keep generic `CutsceneScene` transition payload tests separate from the
  Playwright visual/input flow.

## Companion Testing

- Use deterministic companion creation at explicit hero levels; verify
  independent inventory objects and level-tier loadouts.
- Test quest completion replay, reload, debug completion, and repeated replay
  against the same unique recruited-ID guard.
- Parameterize those paths across Guardian, Scout, and Mystic; one companion
  path is not representative coverage.
- Construct `BattleActionSource`/`PartyCombatant` adapters and verify HP/MP
  writes reach the underlying companion state.
- Test gambits as pure rank/condition/target selection. Invalid rules must not
  mutate action economy, MP, inventory, or effects.
- Cover living-vs-KO XP distribution, level-1 XP floor, party wipe recovery,
  exact defeat receipts, and party-wide inn rest.
- Keep a focused Battle transition regression that asserts fade-complete
  ordering, one-shot scene start, transient cleanup, the full Overworld payload,
  and once-only DefeatScene routing for random and boss encounters without
  rendering Phaser UI.
- Keep Phaser visuals in headless Chromium flows; pure trail positioning and UI
  mutation helpers belong in Vitest.

## Inventory Testing

- Test type/value/rarity/recent/name selectors without mutating canonical order
  or equipment links.
- Cover equipment, consumable, quest, and future crafting filters plus search.
- Normalize and persist `2dnd_inventory_prefs` separately from `2dnd_save`.
- Assert equipped, key-item, mount, and duplicate-item transfer restrictions.
- Use focused Playwright coverage for large-bag keyboard/pointer paging,
  selection stability, search, and menu access.

## Dice Testing Patterns

### Statistical Distribution Testing
```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { rollD20, rollDice, abilityModifier } from "../src/systems/dice";

describe("rollD20 distribution", () => {
  it("returns values between 1 and 20", () => {
    const rolls = Array.from({ length: 200 }, () => rollD20());
    
    expect(Math.min(...rolls)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(Math.max(...rolls)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(20);
  });

  it("produces roughly uniform distribution", () => {
    const rolls = Array.from({ length: 10000 }, () => rollD20());
    const counts = rolls.reduce((acc, roll) => {
      acc[roll] = (acc[roll] || 0) + 1;
      return acc;
    }, {} as Record<number, number>);

    // Each face should appear ~500 times (10000/20)
    // Allow 20% variance (400-600)
    Object.values(counts).forEach(count => {
      expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(400);
      expect(count).toBeLessThan(600);
    });
  });
});
```

### Modifier Calculation Testing
```typescript
describe("abilityModifier", () => {
  it("calculates correct modifiers for standard scores", () => {
    expect(abilityModifier(8)).toBe(-1);
    expect(abilityModifier(10)).toBe(0);
    expect(abilityModifier(11)).toBe(0);
    expect(abilityModifier(12)).toBe(1);
    expect(abilityModifier(16)).toBe(3);
    expect(abilityModifier(20)).toBe(5);
  });

  it("handles edge cases", () => {
    expect(abilityModifier(1)).toBe(-5);
    expect(abilityModifier(3)).toBe(-4);
    expect(abilityModifier(30)).toBe(10);
  });
});
```

## Combat Testing Patterns

### Attack Roll Validation
```typescript
import { calculateAttackRoll, resolveAttack } from "../src/systems/combat";

describe("attack mechanics", () => {
  it("hits when roll meets or exceeds AC", () => {
    const attacker = createTestPlayer({ strength: 16 });  // +3 mod
    const target = createTestMonster({ ac: 13 });
    
    // Mock d20 roll of 10
    const mockRoll = 10;
    const attackBonus = abilityModifier(attacker.stats.strength);
    const total = mockRoll + attackBonus;  // 13
    
    expect(total).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target.ac);
  });

  it("applies critical hit on natural 20", () => {
    const attacker = createTestPlayer();
    const target = createTestMonster({ hp: 50 });
    
    const normalDamage = resolveDamage(attacker, false);
    const criticalDamage = resolveDamage(attacker, true);
    
    // Critical should deal more damage
    expect(criticalDamage).toBeGreaterThan(normalDamage);
  });
});
```

### Damage Calculation Testing
```typescript
describe("damage calculation", () => {
  it("adds ability modifier to weapon damage", () => {
    const attacker = createTestPlayer({ 
      strength: 18,  // +4 modifier
      equipment: { weapon: { damage: "1d8" } }
    });
    
    // Test multiple rolls
    const damages = Array.from({ length: 100 }, () => 
      calculateDamage(attacker)
    );
    
    // Minimum: 1 (min roll) + 4 (modifier) = 5
    // Maximum: 8 (max roll) + 4 (modifier) = 12
    expect(Math.min(...damages)).toBe(5);
    expect(Math.max(...damages)).toBe(12);
  });
});
```

## Player System Testing

### Leveling Logic
```typescript
import { gainXP, levelUp, calculateMaxHP } from "../src/systems/player";

describe("player leveling", () => {
  it("levels up when reaching XP threshold", () => {
```

## Running Tests

### Command Line
```bash
# Run all tests once
npm test

# Install Chromium once, then run the campaign browser suite
npm run test:browser:install
npm run test:browser

# Build and run the Electron smoke suite
npm run test:desktop

# Watch mode (re-run on changes)
npm run test:watch

# Type checking
npm run typecheck

# Production bundle/startup/memory/save baseline
npm run benchmark:baseline

# Run specific test file
npx vitest run tests/dice.test.ts
```

## Browser Golden Path

- `playwright.config.ts` starts Vite on an unused strict localhost port.
- Browser tests default to `/2dnd/`; the showcase test opens that root and
  Phaser tests open `game.html`. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_PATH=/` to reproduce the
  root-base development path.
- Cover the showcase's Play/download links, game-generated screenshots,
  responsive width, Steam banner, and page/console cleanliness.
- Pull request CI installs Chromium and runs the browser suite as a release
  gate.
- Keep trace action logs, DOM snapshots, sources, and failure screenshots, but
  disable trace screenshots and video. Phaser repaints every frame, so the
  filmstrip creates thousands of canvas captures that stall context teardown.
- Use `#debug-state`, `#debug-log`, and persisted save state as authoritative
  synchronization surfaces. Canvas text is not DOM text.
- Registered Phaser layout groups expose bounds and audit results through
  `#layout-report`, `data-layout-overlap-count`, and
  `data-layout-clipping-count`; use stable `layoutId` values instead of brittle
  coordinate-only clicks.
- Hold frame-polled keys with `keyboard.down()`, wait across frames, then
  `keyboard.up()`. Do not use instantaneous presses for Overworld or Ending
  actions.
- Seed randomness before the game loads and assert both `pageerror` and
  `console.error` remain empty.
- Run `npm run benchmark:baseline` before performance-affecting work and attach
  its commit, environment, and output to the owning issue or pull request. The
  harness uses the named `2dnd:boot-textures` browser performance measure and a
  fresh schema-v17 save.
- Cover random and boss defeat results, exact displayed penalties, clean
  continuation, and recovered save/reload state through the production
  `/defeat` debug path.
- Debug commands may accelerate setup, but the final Elowen interaction and
  other behavior under test must still run through their production paths.
- Cover interrupted opening recovery, dungeon reveals, skipped boss
  introductions, aftermath chaining, Chronicle replay immutability, interrupted
  and legacy ending recovery, durable post-game reload, and corrupt-save
  fallback to a usable New Game path.

## Desktop Golden Path

- Build with the relative desktop Vite mode and compiled main/preload process.
- Launch with a fresh explicit test-only Electron user-data directory.
- Assert `location.origin === "app://2dnd"`, the `game.html` entry, and the
  fullscreen bridge shape.
- Create a character through production controls, then close and relaunch the
  shell and continue the same schema-v17 campaign.
- Return to title through the keyboard menu, quit through the visible title
  action, and verify lifecycle/quit logs without save-content leakage.
- Run on macOS, Windows, and Linux CI; use Xvfb only on Linux.
- Never weaken sandbox, navigation, IPC, CSP, or network policy for tests.

### Test Coverage
```bash
# Generate coverage report
npx vitest run --coverage
```

## Best Practices

1. **Test behavior, not implementation** - Focus on inputs/outputs
2. **Use descriptive test names** - "it calculates X when Y"
3. **Arrange-Act-Assert pattern** - Setup, execute, verify
4. **Avoid magic numbers** - Use named constants
5. **Test edge cases** - Zero, negative, maximum values
6. **Mock randomness when needed** - Make tests deterministic
7. **Keep tests fast** - Avoid delays, network calls
8. **One assertion per test (when possible)** - Makes failures clear
9. **Inject group RNG** - Initiative, weighted generation, and random-two
   targeting helpers accept deterministic random functions

## Common Pitfalls

❌ Testing Phaser objects directly (use pure functions)
❌ Relying on random values without bounds checking
❌ Not testing edge cases (0, negative, null)
❌ Tests that depend on execution order
❌ Overly complex test setup
❌ Not cleaning up state between tests

## Related Files

- Test files: `tests/*.test.ts`
- Vitest config: `vitest.config.ts`
- TypeScript config: `tsconfig.json`

<skill-context name="accessibility-keyboard">

# Keyboard Accessibility

You are an expert in keyboard accessibility. Help developers create interfaces that work fully without a mouse.

## Core Requirements

### All Functionality Available
Every interactive feature must be keyboard-operable:
- Navigation and menus
- Buttons and links
- Form inputs
- Sliders and controls
- Modal dialogs
- Drag and drop (alternative required)

### Focus Must Be Visible
Users must see where focus currently is:
- Don't remove default focus outlines without replacement
- Custom focus styles should be high contrast
- Focus should never become invisible

### No Keyboard Traps
Focus must be able to leave any component:
- Can always Tab or Shift+Tab away
- Modals are exception: trap focus inside, but Escape exits

### Logical Focus Order
Tab order follows visual/reading order:
- Left to right, top to bottom (for LTR languages)
- Avoid positive tabindex values
- Let DOM order determine focus order

## Focus Management

### When to Manage Focus
- Opening/closing modals (move into, restore on close)
- Loading new content dynamically
- Deleting items (where should focus go?)
- Single-page navigation (move to new content)
- Error messages (optionally focus error)

### tabindex Values

**tabindex="0"**
Makes element focusable in natural order.
Use for custom interactive elements.

**tabindex="-1"**
Focusable programmatically but not via Tab.
Use for focus management targets.

**tabindex="1+"**
Avoid! Creates unpredictable order.
Rearrange DOM instead.

## Skip Links

### Purpose
Let keyboard users bypass repetitive content (nav menus).

### Implementation
- Place at very top of page
- Link targets main content
- Visible on focus (can be visually hidden until focused)
- Text like "Skip to main content"

### Target
Main content area should have:
- Meaningful heading or landmark
- tabindex="-1" to receive focus (if not focusable)
- Ideally an ID to link to

## Focus Indicators

### Requirements
- Visible in all color modes
- Sufficient contrast against background
- Not reliant on color alone
- At least 2px solid outline recommended

### Techniques
- CSS outline (doesn't affect layout)
- Box shadow for rounded corners
- Combination of outline and offset
- Background color change WITH outline

### Focus-Visible
Use :focus-visible to show focus only for keyboard:
- Hides focus ring for mouse clicks
- Shows for keyboard navigation
- Better visual experience

## Widget Keyboard Patterns

### Single Tab Stop Components
Complex widgets should be one tab stop:
- Tab into the widget
- Arrow keys navigate within
- Tab out to next component

Examples: tab lists, menus, toolbars, tree views

### Menu Navigation
- Arrow Up/Down to move through items
- Enter or Space to select
- Escape to close
- Home/End to jump to first/last

### Tabs Navigation
- Tab to reach tab list
- Arrow Left/Right between tabs
- Tab to reach panel content
- Activate on arrow (immediate) or Enter (delayed)

### Modal Dialogs
- Focus first interactive element on open
- Tab cycles within modal (trap)
- Escape closes modal
- Return focus to trigger on close

## Common Keyboard Issues

### Invisible Focus
Focus indicator removed or same color as background.
Fix: Add visible :focus styles.

### Focus Lost
After action, focus disappears or moves unexpectedly.
Fix: Programmatically manage focus after DOM changes.

### Wrong Tab Order
Tab jumps around illogically.
Fix: Adjust DOM order or use tabindex carefully.

### Mouse-Only Features
Dropdowns, carousels, drag-drop work only with mouse.
Fix: Add keyboard alternatives (arrow keys, buttons).

### Positive Tabindex
Tab order doesn't match visual order.
Fix: Remove positive tabindex, use DOM order.

## Testing Keyboard Access

### Basic Test
1. Put away the mouse
2. Start at browser address bar
3. Tab through entire page
4. Reach every interactive element
5. Operate every feature

### What to Check
- Can you see where focus is?
- Does order make sense?
- Can you activate everything?
- Can you always escape/return?

## Workflow

1. Audit all interactive features
2. Test each with keyboard only
3. Add/fix focus indicators
4. Implement skip links
5. Add focus management for dynamic content
6. Use proper tabindex values
7. Test full keyboard journey

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All features work keyboard-only
- [ ] Focus always visible
- [ ] No keyboard traps
- [ ] Tab order is logical
- [ ] Skip links present
- [ ] Focus managed for dynamic content
- [ ] Widgets follow expected patterns

</skill-context>

# ARIA Implementation

You are an expert in ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications). Help developers use ARIA correctly to make dynamic content accessible.

## ARIA First Rule

**Don't use ARIA if native HTML works.**

Native HTML elements have built-in accessibility:
- Use `<button>` not `<div role="button">`
- Use `<nav>` not `<div role="navigation">`
- Use `<input type="checkbox">` not custom ARIA checkbox

Only use ARIA when native HTML is insufficient.

## ARIA Categories

### Roles
Define what an element IS.
- widget roles: button, checkbox, slider, tablist
- document structure: article, heading, list
- landmark roles: banner, main, navigation, contentinfo

### States
Current condition that may change.
- aria-checked, aria-expanded, aria-selected
- aria-disabled, aria-hidden, aria-invalid
- Update with JavaScript when state changes

### Properties
Characteristics that are generally stable.
- aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby
- aria-required, aria-readonly
- aria-haspopup, aria-controls

## Common Widget Patterns

### Button
Native `<button>` preferred. If must use div:
- role="button"
- tabindex="0"
- Handle Enter and Space key events
- Update aria-pressed for toggle buttons

### Checkbox
Native `<input type="checkbox">` preferred. If custom:
- role="checkbox"
- aria-checked="true" or "false" or "mixed"
- tabindex="0"
- Toggle with Space key

### Dialog/Modal
- role="dialog" or role="alertdialog"
- aria-modal="true"
- aria-labelledby pointing to title
- Focus management: trap focus inside, return on close

### Tabs
- role="tablist" on container
- role="tab" on tab buttons
- role="tabpanel" on panels
- aria-selected on active tab
- aria-controls linking tab to panel

### Menu
- role="menu" on container
- role="menuitem" on items
- Arrow key navigation
- aria-expanded on trigger if dropdown

### Accordion
- Button triggers with aria-expanded
- aria-controls linking to content
- Hidden content with aria-hidden or hidden attribute

## Live Regions

Announce dynamic content changes to screen readers.

### aria-live
- "polite": Announce when user is idle
- "assertive": Announce immediately (use sparingly)

### aria-atomic
- "true": Announce entire region
- "false": Announce only changed parts

### Specialized Live Regions
- role="alert": Assertive announcement
- role="status": Polite announcement (like aria-live="polite")
- role="log": Append-only updates
- role="timer": Time updates

## Labeling

### aria-label
Direct text label. Use when visible label isn't present.
Example: `<button aria-label="Close">`

### aria-labelledby
Reference visible element(s) as label.
Example: `<div aria-labelledby="heading1 heading2">`

### aria-describedby
Reference element providing additional description.
Example: `<input aria-describedby="help-text">`

## Hiding Content

### aria-hidden="true"
Hides from assistive tech but visible on screen.
Use for decorative elements, icons with text labels.
Never hide focusable elements.

### hidden attribute
Hides from everyone (visual and assistive tech).
Use for content not currently relevant.

### Visually hidden (CSS)
Visible to screen readers, hidden visually.
For skip links, extra context for screen readers.

## Common Mistakes

### ARIA Overload
Adding unnecessary ARIA to elements that don't need it.
Native HTML already has semantics.

### Role Without Behavior
Adding role="button" without keyboard handling.
Role changes announcement, not functionality.

### Static aria-live
Content already present when page loads doesn't need live region.
Live regions are for dynamic changes.

### Broken References
aria-labelledby or aria-describedby pointing to non-existent IDs.
Always verify ID references exist.

### Hiding Content Incorrectly
Using aria-hidden="true" on focusable elements.
Focus still reaches them, causing confusion.

## Testing ARIA

### Screen Reader Testing
- Does content announce correctly?
- Are states announced when they change?
- Are labels and descriptions read?

### Developer Tools
- Accessibility inspector in browser DevTools
- Check computed accessible name
- Verify role and states

## Workflow

1. Use native HTML elements when possible
2. Identify what role/behavior is needed
3. Add appropriate ARIA role
4. Add required states and properties
5. Implement keyboard interaction
6. Update states with JavaScript
7. Test with screen reader

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Native HTML used when sufficient
- [ ] Roles match actual behavior
- [ ] States updated dynamically
- [ ] Labels properly associated
- [ ] Keyboard interaction implemented
- [ ] Screen reader announces correctly
- [ ] ID references are valid

5. ## The adventure
6. 
7. 2D&D is a browser JRPG built around exploration, party growth, turn-based
8. combat, and a complete campaign. Create a hero from 12 classes, travel through
9. the 90-chunk world, recruit up to three active companions, restore three
10. keystones, and return to Elowen to complete the Twelvefold Covenant.
11. 
12. The campaign includes seven chapters, 12 mainland cities, connected districts,
13. three campaign dungeons, story and boss cutscenes, optional objectives, an
14. epilogue, credits, Chronicle replay, and post-game continuation. Tidehaven and
15. the Deepwake Kraken form an optional island and sea-navigation arc.
16. 
17. ## Core controls
18. 
19. Feature-specific shortcuts become available only after the corresponding
20. system has been discovered. The Escape menu remains the reliable entry point.
21. 
22. | Keyboard | Action |
23. | --- | --- |
24. | `WASD` / arrows | Move, navigate menus, cycle valid Battle targets |
25. | `Space` / `Enter` | Confirm, interact, or disarm a detected adjacent trap |
26. | `Esc` | Open the in-game menu, cancel/close an overlay, or skip a cutscene |
27. | `F1` | Open Tips |
28. | `M` | Open the map |
29. | `E` | Open equipment |
30. | `Q` | Open the quest journal after discovery |
31. | `P` | Open party management after recruiting a companion |
32. | `C` | Open the Codex after discovery |
33. | `Y` | Open Achievements after the first natural unlock |
34. | `K` | Open Gathering after discovering a discipline |
35. | `V` | Open Crafting after learning a non-starting recipe |
36. | `T` | Mount or dismount after acquiring a mount |
37. 
38. Pointer and touch users can select visible buttons directly. Touch layouts use
39. safe-area-aware movement and action controls. Standard gamepads use the left
40. stick or D-pad for movement/navigation, `A` to confirm, `B` to cancel, `X` to
41. interact, Menu/`Y` for the menu, View for Tips, bumpers for targets/pages, and
42. triggers for Battle-log scrolling. The right stick moves a visible cursor;
43. press the stick to click pointer-first controls.
44. 
45. Mappings are stable rather than user-remappable. Settings can control touch
46. visibility, handedness, and automatic or fixed prompt sources.
47. 
48. The in-game menu includes **Save & Return to Title**. Desktop builds also show
49. **Quit Desktop** on the title screen, with `Q` as a title-screen shortcut.
50. Browser builds rely on the browser tab/window controls instead.
51. 
52. ## Character creation and progression
53. 
54. Character creation follows:
55. 
56. **Name -> Class -> Stats -> Appearance -> Adventure**
57. 
58. - Choose Knight, Ranger, Wizard, Sorcerer, Rogue, Paladin, Warlock, Cleric,
59.   Druid, Barbarian, Monk, or Bard.
60. - Spend 27 points on base scores from 8 to 15, or use 4d6-drop-lowest random
61.   generation.
62. - Class boosts apply after base stats.
63. - Level progression reaches 20 with class actions, spells, talents, equipment,
64.   hit-point growth, proficiency increases, and ability-score improvements.

66. ## Party, inventory, and gambits
67. 
68. Guardian, Scout, and Mystic join through their own quests. Recruited companions
69. have independent levels, stats, HP/MP, equipment, inventories, abilities,
70. spells, status effects, and control settings. Up to three active companions
71. follow the hero without blocking movement or triggering world interactions.
72. 
73. Party members can be controlled manually or by up to 12 ranked gambit rules.
74. Gambits evaluate a fresh turn snapshot, skip invalid rules without spending
75. resources, and can use one bonus action plus one main action.
76. 
77. See [Companions and gambits](companions.md) and
78. [Inventory presentation](inventory.md).

80. ## Combat
81. 
82. Battles use d20 attacks, Dexterity initiative, natural 1/20 attack outcomes,
83. critical hits, Armor Class, defending, fleeing, spells, abilities, items, and
84. boss actions. Encounters contain one to four independent enemies with stable
85. initiative identities and front/back formations.
86. 
87. Nine elements are supported: Fire, Ice, Lightning, Poison, Necrotic, Radiant,
88. Thunder, Force, and Psychic. Immunities prevent damage, weaknesses double it,
89. and resistances halve it. Observed interactions become Codex knowledge.
90. 
91. Combat statuses include Poisoned, Burning, Frozen, Paralyzed, Stunned,
92. Frightened, Slowed, Prone, Asleep, Confused, Enraged, Hasted, Inspired, Raging,
93. and Sneak Stance. Effects resolve on actor turn boundaries and are cleared when
94. Battle ends.
95. 
96. A full party wipe applies one recovery result, autosaves it, reports exact gold
97. and XP losses, clears Battle effects, and returns the party to the last town at
98. half HP/MP.

791. 
792. Save schema version is 17.
793. 
794. Schema v17 adds normalized feature-discovery IDs, pending one-time reveal IDs,
795. explicit debug reveals, and debug-suppressed evidence. Schema-v16 and older
796. saves start with empty discovery metadata and silently reconcile all durable
797. authoritative evidence, so mature saves regain earned menus without replaying
798. rewards or showing reveal storms.
799. 
800. Electron persists the same documents through the stable `app://2dnd` origin.
801. The native shell never owns or mutates campaign state, and browser/desktop
802. origins never silently merge.
803. Desktop lifecycle and failures append to bounded rotating logs below Electron
804. user data without recording save payloads. Save & Return to Title autosaves
805. before Boot; application quit is exposed only on the desktop title screen
806. through trusted zero-argument IPC.
807. 
808. Schema v16 adds `player.progression.nautical`: typed boat ownership, condition,
809. upgrades and cosmetics; discovered ports, routes, islands, continents, and sea
810. fog keys; bounded navigation statistics; and recoverable pending merchant
811. routes, hazards, and encounters. Canonical continent/zone/port/island metadata
812. is derived and never persisted. Invalid sailing locations recover to a safe
813. known port or Willowdale without renumbering legacy chunks or changing
814. level-zero/chunk-zero fog formats.
815. 
816. `loadGame()` treats parsed data as `unknown`, migrates legacy flat position and
817. progression fields, normalizes active effects, Codex elements, and skill-check
818. records, validates city/dungeon IDs and quest state, clamps levels/districts,
819. repairs invalid coordinates to the correct spawn, and falls back to Willowdale
820. for unusable overworld locations. Schema-v3 skill-check saves gain default
821. quest state. Flat schema-v4 Ashen Road saves migrate to nested Covenant
822. objective/reward/warning state without replaying completed rewards.
823. Schema-v3 skill-check and schema-v4 quest saves gain explicit trap defaults.
824. If a malformed trap seed is replaced,
825. `trapStates` is cleared so stale IDs cannot resolve against a different layout.
826. Schema-v5 saves gain an empty `player.party`; party normalization validates
827. companion IDs, active order, resources, known actions, canonical inventory,
828. equipment links, effects, control mode, dialogue state, and gambits before
829. replaying completed recruitment actions.
830. Schema-v6 and older saves gain an empty `seenCutsceneIds` list. Cutscene
831. normalization keeps only known stable IDs and removes malformed or duplicate
832. entries. Schema-v7 and older saves gain an empty `pendingCutsceneIds` list;
833. normalization removes unknown, duplicate, malformed, or already-seen IDs.
834. Legacy recovery queues only a completed-but-unseen epilogue. Pre-v9 saves gain
835. `{ completed: true }` tutorial progress so established campaigns are not
836. interrupted; malformed v9 completion values normalize to false.
837. Schema-v9 and older monster-only Codex data gains normalized
838. `unlockedEntryIds`; unknown, malformed, and duplicate IDs are removed, valid
839. monster discovery is preserved, and durable player evidence is replayed
840. idempotently to recover world knowledge.
841. Schema-v10 and older saves gain default World Event state. Event normalization
842. validates the seed, counters, known event/choice IDs, pending phase/location,
843. repeat counters, claimed/resolved IDs, and bounded record. Replacing a malformed
844. seed clears the pending event so it cannot resolve against corrupt state.
845. Schema-v11 and older saves gain the exact Chaotic Neutral baseline and neutral
846. reputation. Do not replay historical social outcomes; mark deterministic quest
847. social sources consumed while preserving existing quest/reward/Codex/event state.
848. Schema-v12 and older saves gain normalized achievement state and silently
849. reconcile reconstructable milestones. Their defeat history remains explicitly
850. unknown, preventing retroactive no-defeat credit. Unknown/duplicate achievement
851. or title IDs are removed, counters are clamped, completion order is repaired,
852. pending notices must reference earned achievements, and equipped titles must be
853. unlocked.
854. Schema-v13 and older saves gain default deterministic gathering state. Schema-v14
855. normalization validates discipline/resource/outcome IDs, patterns, locations,
856. statistics, cooldowns, claimed IDs, and bounded history. Replacing a malformed
857. gathering seed clears node state, discovered generated nodes, and pending play.
858. Schema-v14 and older saves gain default crafting state. Schema-v15 normalization
859. keeps known canonical recipes, deduplicates discovery and transaction IDs,
860. clamps natural statistics and per-recipe counts, bounds/repairs recent history,
861. preserves prior gathering/inventory/equipment/achievement state, and replays
862. durable recipe discovery idempotently.
863. 
864. Inventory presentation preferences are not save ownership data and do not
865. increment the schema. Store them under `2dnd_inventory_prefs`.
866. Audio and accessibility preferences are not campaign save fields. The versioned
867. `2dnd_preferences` document is normalized by `src/systems/accessibility.ts`,
868. migrates the legacy audio and cutscene-accessibility keys, and notifies live
869. title/in-game settings consumers immediately.
870. 
871. When persistent data changes:
872. 
873. 1. Update its interface and creation default.
874. 2. Add runtime normalization and cross-field validation.
875. 3. Increment the schema version when the shape changes.

# Code Review: Issue #166 — Multiple Save Slots & Storage Recovery

I inspected the full uncommitted diff and relevant existing code, ran `typecheck` (passes) and the 5 save-related unit suites (73 pass), and **empirically confirmed** the input findings below with temporary Playwright probes (since removed). Most focus areas are solid; two real input bugs were found.

## What I verified as correct (no issue)
`saveStorage.ts` atomic write/rollback/recovery ordering (primary→staging→backup); migration idempotence (`SAVE_SLOT_MIGRATION_KEY` guard, autosave aliases legacy `2dnd_save`); manual-slot key isolation; loading a manual slot into autosave; playtime object-identity across `loadGame`→Overworld; import validation (rejects version > `SAVE_VERSION`, non-integer, negative); Boot new-game overwrite confirmation (no longer eagerly `deleteSave()`); scene cleanup on shutdown. These need no changes.

---

## Blocking

### 1. Closing the Overworld save menu with SPACE (or gamepad/touch "confirm") leaks a world action that gets autosaved
**Evidence (empirically confirmed):** Seeded a hero standing on the Heartlands Crypt exit tile, opened the save menu (ESC→Save Game), navigated to **close**, and pressed Space. Result: the menu closed **and** the player exited the dungeon (`[DUNGEON:heartlands_dungeon]` disappeared, hero moved to the entrance tile). `LEAK_ON_CLOSE: YES`.

**Root cause:**
- Overworld processes world actions by polling `Phaser.Input.Keyboard.JustDown(this.keys.SPACE)` in `update()` and calling `handleAction()` — deliberately *before* the overlay guard (`src/scenes/Overworld.ts:2027-2034`).
- `handleAction()` guards with `if (this.saveSlotManager.isOpen()) return;` (`Overworld.ts:2396`), but `SaveSlotManager.handleKeyDown` activates the action and **closes synchronously on the keydown** (`src/managers/saveSlots.ts:487-490`). By the time the same-frame `JustDown` poll runs, the manager is already closed, so the guard passes and the world action fires.
- `event.stopImmediatePropagation()` (saveSlots.ts:489) cannot stop a *polled* `JustDown` read, so it provides no protection here. (This is why **Boot is safe** — its continue path is the event-driven `keydown-SPACE` listener, which `stopImmediatePropagation` *does* suppress; I confirmed Boot does not leak.)
- Gamepad and touch "confirm" both synthesize a real `Space` keydown dispatched to `window` (`ACTION_KEYS.confirm = {code:"Space"}` at `src/managers/input.ts:45`; dispatched at `input.ts:486` and `input.ts:379-380`), so **all three input methods** hit the identical leak. Only ENTER-close and ESC-close are safe (Overworld never polls those).

**Impact:** The normal "close" gesture can silently trigger a state-changing world action — exit a dungeon, enter a city, open a one-time chest, board a boat, or start a boss battle — and each path calls `autoSave()`, **persisting the unintended state**. This is a data-integrity regression reachable through ordinary keyboard/controller/touch use.

**Suggested fix:** Adopt the established mitigation the ESC menu already uses — defer Enter/Space *activation* to keyup instead of acting on keydown. See `src/managers/overlay.ts:1165-1187`, which does `preventDefault()` + `stopImmediatePropagation()` on the keydown and then `keyboard.once("keyup-SPACE"/"keyup-ENTER", activate)`. Applying the same pattern in `SaveSlotManager.handleKeyDown` keeps the manager open during the keydown frame (so `handleAction`'s guard suppresses the poll) and closes on keyup (when `JustDown` won't re-fire). This also fixes the gamepad/touch vectors, whose keyup arrives on a later tick.

---

## Non-Blocking

### 2. Feature hotkey C (Codex) fires through the open Overworld save menu
**Evidence (empirically confirmed):** With the Overworld save menu open, pressing **C** launched `CodexScene` and abandoned the save menu (`CODEX_LEAK: YES`, `SAVE_MENU_STILL_OPEN: no`).

**Root cause:** `openCodex()` (`Overworld.ts:3382-3400`) and the `cKey` handler (`Overworld.ts:866-878`) check many overlays but not `saveSlotManager.isOpen()`. The manager only calls `stopImmediatePropagation()` for Escape and Enter/Space (`saveSlots.ts:440, 489`); for any other key it returns at `saveSlots.ts:487` without stopping propagation, so the feature key reaches its `Key.on("down")` handler.

**Scope note:** The equip key `E` handler (`Overworld.ts:900-908`) has the same missing guard and is likely affected (I could not confirm it — the equip overlay has no debug marker). The achievements key `Y` (`Overworld.ts:881-898`) did **not** leak in testing (incidentally blocked), so guarding is currently inconsistent across feature keys.

**Impact:** Pressing a feature hotkey while the save menu is open yanks the player out of the menu (for C, into a whole scene) without completing their save intent. Lower severity than #1 (no data loss; `openCodex` autosaves), but it's a real input-isolation bug.

**Suggested fix:** Add `if (this.saveSlotManager.isOpen()) return;` (or a shared `isOverlayOpen()`-style check that already includes the save menu — note `Overworld.ts:1494-1505` includes it) to the C/E/Y feature-key handlers, or guard inside `openCodex`/`openAchievements`/`toggleEquipOverlay`, consistent with how `handleAction` already guards at `Overworld.ts:2396`.

---

## Suggestion

### 3. Test gap that would have caught both bugs
`e2e/save-slots.spec.ts` only ever closes the Overworld save menu via **cancel/Escape**, and never presses a feature key while the menu is open. Both bugs above survive precisely because no test exercises (a) SPACE-closing the Overworld save menu while standing on an interactive tile, or (b) pressing C/E/Y over the open save menu. Recommend adding an e2e case that opens the Overworld save menu on an interactive tile (e.g., dungeon exit or boss lair), closes it with **Space** (via `keyboard.down/up`, not the too-fast `press`), and asserts no world action fired; plus one that presses a feature hotkey and asserts the save menu stays open and no scene change occurs.

---

**Note on methodology:** The empirical `press("Space")` fast path can miss the polled `JustDown`; reliable reproduction requires `keyboard.down("Space")` → wait a frame → `up("Space")`. Any regression test for #1 should use that form or it may spuriously pass.

The review found two modal-input leaks: Space-close could trigger a world interaction, and feature hotkeys could escape the save dialog. I’m applying keyup activation plus explicit shortcut guards, then adding regressions.

input.title: Add resilient multiple save slots
input.body:
Closes #166

## Summary

- add schema-v18 playtime metadata, a dedicated autosave, three named manual slots, atomic staging writes, prior-primary backups, and per-slot corruption recovery
- preserve and verify legacy `2dnd_save` campaigns in place; keep manual snapshots isolated when loading, saving, copying, renaming, deleting, importing, or exporting
- add shared accessible title/Overworld slot management with explicit overwrite/delete confirmation and keyboard, pointer, touch, and gamepad support
- surface storage failures visibly and update browser, Electron, migration, documentation, and roadmap contracts

## Validation

- `npm ci` and `npm audit` — 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test` — 982 tests
- `npm run test:browser` — 30 tests
- `npm run test:desktop` — 1 production-like Electron flow
- `npm run build`
- `npm run build:desktop`
- `git diff --check`

## Performance baseline

Same Apple M3 / Node 26 / Chromium 151 environment, 20 cache-disabled samples per startup case.

| Metric | Base `c793201` (schema v17) | This branch `ce3b734` (schema v18) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Empty-save title median | 384.6 ms | 373.9 ms |
| Fresh-save title median | 399.5 ms | 389.7 ms |
| Boot textures median | 27.3 / 27.6 ms | 26.2 / 26.1 ms |
| JS listeners | 114 | 114 |
| Fresh save size | 4.27 KiB | 4.29 KiB |
| Save write median / p95 | 0.018 / 0.025 ms | 0.013 / 0.015 ms |
| JavaScript gzip | 618.53 KiB | 626.13 KiB |
